messages.subject: Problem running Distance v6.2 r1
parts:
Dear List

 

I’m new to this branch of statistics, having recently chased down text books on the subject and downloaded the Distance software.

 

I’m on a government network (which may explain my problem), and had to use my administrator privilege to install Distance. All seems to have gone well, with the install going into the 32-bit directory C:\Program Files (x86).  

 

The software opens OK, and I have started at the beginning by trying to walk through the worked examples, starting with Line Transect Example.dst. I can view the data structure of this example OK, but running the Analyses tab brings up the following error message. Does anyone have any advice on what it means please?

 

Also, when I try to uninstall the software, again as an administrator, I get the message “Could not open INSTALL.LOG file”, and yet I can see the text file (and open it) in C:\PROGRAM FILES (x86)\Distance 6\

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Problem running Distance v6.2 r1
parts:
Terry:

I had this email conversation with a government employee in the U.S. just yesterday on the very same problem.

You may have administrator privilege to install the program, but I suspect you also need such privilege to run the program.  If you install and run the software on a personal machine without the added security, the program will work just fine.  Notice you encounter the error at run-time; are you in a position to give yourself administrator privilege for running as well as installing?

messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] Problem running Distance v6.2 r1
parts:
Eric

 

Many thanks for your prompt reply.

 

You are correct, over the weekend I successfully installed and ran the first worked example on my personal PC without any errors whatsoever.

 

However, just now I logged onto my work PC as an ‘administrator’, reinstalled Distance, but running the first example brought up the same error message as before. It would seem to me that there are various levels of ‘administrator’ status, and I need a higher one. I’ll chase this up with my IT department and report back.

 

Regards, Terry
